title: JobSpec
description: Any unit of work in the system: what to do, to which inputs, with which parameters, how far it got, and how to pick it up again.
$comment:
Kill the app at 47% of a 3TB scan; on relaunch it continues. That single requirement drives every design choice here.

 IDEMPOTENCY: job_id is a BLAKE3 over (job_type, ordered input hashes, source_locator_digest, params_digest, scope). Submitting the same work twice yields the same id, so 'have we already done this' is a primary-key lookup rather than a heuristic. Re-running a completed job is a no-op by construction, not by convention.

 THE SOURCE-LOCATOR DIGEST EXISTS FOR ONE JOB TYPE. scan_source runs BEFORE anything has a content hash -- discovering files is what produces them -- so its `media_ids` are empty and the rest of the identity tuple is identical for every scan with the same parameters. Two different folders would then collide on job_id, and the second scan would be treated as already done: a whole drive silently never imported. source_locator_digest folds the canonicalised source roots into the identity so distinct roots are distinct jobs. It is required for scan_source and meaningless elsewhere, where content hashes already carry the identity.

 RESUMPTION: `checkpoint.cursor` is deliberately an opaque string owned by the worker. The contract guarantees that it is durably stored and handed back on resume; it does not presume to know what a file walker or an FFmpeg pass needs to remember. What the contract DOES specify is that partial outputs are recorded as they are produced, so resumption never redoes completed sub-work.

 EGRESS: a job whose `requires_egress` is true MUST carry a ConsentRef. This is checked in the schema, not only in code, because 'no network egress without a consent-ledger entry' is verified by an automated CI test and the contract is where that promise is made legible.

job_id.description: BLAKE3 over (job_type, sorted input ids, source_locator_digest or the empty string, params_digest, scope). Doubles as the idempotency key -- there is deliberately no second field for that, because two sources of truth for identity is how duplicate work gets in.

job_type.description: What kind of work. Enumerated rather than free-form so that a worker cannot be handed a job type it has never heard of and improvise.

params.description: Type-specific parameters. Free-form because the parameter shape of `plan_reel` and `hash_file` have nothing in common, but never anonymous: params_digest pins it. A worker validates its own params against its own local schema.

params_digest.description: BLAKE3 over the canonical JSON of `params`. Part of job_id, which is what makes 'same job with different settings' a genuinely different job rather than a silent overwrite of the first result.

scope.description: Namespace separating otherwise-identical work: a library id, a project id, or a user id. Without it, two users analysing the same stock photo would collide on job_id.

priority.description: Higher runs first. Interactive work (the user is watching a progress bar) outranks background sweeps.

allOf.$comment: A scan has no content hashes yet, so without a source-locator digest two scans of different drives share an identity and the second is skipped as already-done. Requiring both the paths and their digest makes that collision unrepresentable.

JobInputs.title: JobInputs
JobInputs.description: Everything the job reads, addressed by hash. Content addressing is what makes the whole pipeline idempotent: identical inputs cannot produce a different job.

media_ids.description: Sorted before hashing into job_id, so input order never changes job identity.

source_paths.description: Only for scan_source, which by definition starts before anything has a hash. Every other job type addresses content, never location.

source_locator_digest.description: BLAKE3 over the canonical form of `source_paths`: each path resolved to absolute, symlinks followed, trailing separators stripped, NFC-normalised, then sorted and joined with a NUL separator. Required for scan_source and the only thing distinguishing two scans of different folders, since neither has content hashes yet. Canonicalisation matters as much as the digest -- '/Volumes/Archive' and '/Volumes/Archive/' must not be two jobs, or a re-scan re-walks a whole drive.

parent_job_id.description: The job that spawned this one. A scan spawns a hash job per file; the tree is what makes 'cancel this import' a well-defined operation.

depends_on_job_ids.description: Jobs that must reach completed before this one may start.

models.description: Model pins. Part of the params digest, so re-running with a swapped model is a different job and the old result is never silently reused.

JobRequirements.title: JobRequirements
JobRequirements.description: What the job needs to run. The scheduler matches these against the machine rather than discovering mid-render that there is no GPU.

hardware_decode.description: Proxy generation must saturate disk I/O rather than CPU, which is only possible with VideoToolbox/NVDEC/QSV. A proxy job that would fall back to software decode should queue rather than crawl.

requires_source_file.description: True only for proxy generation and final render. Everything else works on proxies -- sources are opened exactly twice in a file's life.

EgressDeclaration.title: EgressDeclaration
EgressDeclaration.description: Whether this job talks to the network, and on whose authority. Declared on every job including the overwhelming majority that declare `false`, because an absent declaration and a negative one must not look the same.

payload_kind.description: What actually leaves the device. `contact_sheet` and `thumbnail` are the only image-bearing values permitted for Tier 3, and `original_media` requires its own explicit consent scope -- originals never leave without one.

allOf.$comment: The contract-level expression of 'no network egress without a consent-ledger entry'. A job that wants the network must name its consent, its destination and what it is sending.

status.description: `paused` is a deliberate user action; `pending` after a crash is what a killed `running` job becomes on relaunch. Distinguishing them is what makes resumption safe -- a paused job must not restart itself.

heartbeat_at.description: Last sign of life. A running job whose heartbeat has gone stale was killed with the process and is safe to reclaim -- without it, a crashed job is indistinguishable from a slow one and blocks its queue forever.

Progress.title: Progress
Progress.description: Progress in real units, not a synthetic percentage. '12,400 of 318,000 files' survives a restart honestly; a percentage that jumps backwards does not.

units_total.description: Null while still being discovered -- a scan does not know how many files exist until it has walked them, and claiming otherwise produces a progress bar that lies.

Checkpoint.title: Checkpoint
Checkpoint.description: Durable resumption state. The cursor is opaque on purpose: the contract promises to persist and return it, and declines to speculate about what a directory walker or a video encoder needs to remember.

resumable.description: False for jobs that must restart from zero -- a short atomic render, say. Stating it explicitly stops a scheduler from assuming either way.

cursor.description: Worker-owned opaque state. Null means 'resumable but not yet started'.

checkpoint_version.description: Bumped when a worker changes its cursor format. A cursor from an older version is discarded and the job restarts, rather than being handed to code that will misparse it.

completed_input_ids.description: Inputs already finished. On resume these are skipped, which is what stops a resumed 3TB scan from rehashing the first 2TB.

partial_output_ids.description: Outputs written before the interruption. Recorded so they are neither orphaned nor recreated.

id.description: Content hash of the produced artifact, so an output can be verified rather than trusted.

message.description: Already redacted: no paths, no filenames, no EXIF. Crash reporting forwards this verbatim, so redaction happens at write time rather than at send time.

failed_input_id.description: Which specific input broke, so a 300k-file scan reports one bad file rather than failing wholesale.

quarantine_after_max.description: Move to quarantined rather than failed once attempts are exhausted, so a hostile file is never retried automatically again but is still visible in the diagnostics view. Nothing is dropped silently.

Journal.title: Journal
Journal.description: Record of every destructive or externally-visible action the job took. 'No silent data loss' means anything irreversible is written down before it happens, not after it succeeds.
